key_insight: Making different biological data types line up is not the same as combining their knowledge. Multimodal cell models must also capture complementary information that becomes useful when data types are considered together.
problem_solved: How to distinguish superficial alignment between biological data types from integration that captures both shared information and complementary insights.
method: Examines whether aligning biological data types is sufficient for meaningful multimodal integration.
Distinguishes information repeated across data types from complementary information they provide.
The supplied abstract does not specify model architectures, datasets, or evaluation procedures.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, alignment alone is an insufficient indicator of successful multimodal learning. Evaluation should also test whether combining modalities adds useful information beyond what each provides separately.
visual_elements: Side-by-side diagrams: aligned data representations versus jointly integrated information.
Overlapping circles showing shared information and distinct contributions from two biological data types.
A conceptual flow diagram showing complementary inputs combining into a richer cell representation.
A checklist contrasting 'modalities align' with 'combined modalities add insight.'
paper_title: Multimodal cell foundation models require synergistic integration beyond alignment
paper_authors: Till Richter, Eric Zimmermann, James Hall, Fabian J. Theis, Srivatsan Raghavan
